name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

writer_notes: Numbers in prose (496 calories, 40.7 g protein, 14 servings) are the locked engine figures from the dispatch. No cost_ps value or cost_lines were supplied, so cost_closing uses the ${{cost_ps}} token and shop_smart makes no per-line cost claims.

Source recipe was small (10.5x7.5 dish, 9 sheets, 3 layers). The locked batch scales about 2.33x to 14 servings, so make_it advises a 13x9 dish or two smaller dishes and preserves the source's 'parsley on the first two layers only' rule.
Pepper is not a separate bought line; it is folded into the 'Salt' buy string (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper) and is used in the blend step, so it is not an orphan.
All 8 bought ingredients are used by a step, and no step uses anything not on the buy list.
Cottage cheese blended with alfredo stands in for ricotta by design; prose must not call it ricotta.

Flag for repair pass: the locked protein is 'Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites' (breaded), while the run condition specifies boneless skinless chicken breast. Prose keeps it neutral ('breaded chicken breast bites') and does not claim plain breast.

prose.intro_html: Lasagna has a reputation as a weekend project, the thing you make when you have a free afternoon and no intention of tracking a single bite. This version rewrites that story. We skip the ricotta and the long-simmered red sauce, blend cottage cheese with alfredo for a creamy layer that hits well above its calorie weight, and stack it with breaded chicken breast bites for the protein. The result is 14 containers of chicken alfredo lasagna at 496 calories and 40.7 grams of protein a serving. That is comfort food that clocks in, sits down, and does the math for you.
prose.shop_smart:
The whole trick to this dish is buying cheap dairy and letting the blender do the fancy part. Here is how I shop it.

  • Cottage cheese is the workhorse. Grab the big low-fat tub, because we are blending it smooth with the alfredo and nobody will ever know it was not ricotta. You need 4 2/3 cups, so buy the family-size container and skip the little cups.
  • Alfredo sauce carries the flavor, so this is the one place to spend a little. A roasted garlic alfredo is worth it. You only need 1 3/4 cups, and blending it into all that cottage cheese makes it go a long way.
  • Buy a block of parmesan and grate it yourself. The pre-shredded stuff in the bag is coated so it will not clump, which is exactly why it never melts right. You need 2 1/3 cups grated, and a block gets you there.
  • Fresh mozzarella gives you those bubbly, browned edges. Shred it rough, no need to be neat about it, since it all melts down anyway.
  • No-boil lasagna sheets save you a pot of boiling water and a colander to wash. Count out 21 sheets so you know the box covers the full batch before you start layering.
  • Frozen breaded chicken breast bites go straight from the freezer to the oven or air fryer, so grab a bag and let the appliance do the cooking.
  • Fresh parsley is a garnish here, not a main event. One bunch is plenty, since you only need 6 tablespoons chopped.
prose.make_it:
Nothing here is hard. It is layering, and the oven does the rest.

  1. Heat the oven to 425 degrees.
  2. Bake or air fry the frozen chicken bites according to the bag. Once they are cooked through, roughly chop them into bite-size pieces and set them aside.
  3. Blend the cottage cheese, the alfredo, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper until it is completely smooth. This blended sauce is what stands in for the ricotta, so take it all the way to creamy.
  4. Coat the bottom of your baking dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce. Lay down 3 noodle sheets, then add another layer of sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the layers until everything is used, finishing the top with mozzarella and parmesan. Only use parsley on the first two layers so it does not turn bitter under the heat. Scaled to 14 servings this is a big bake, so reach for a 13 by 9 dish, or split it across two smaller dishes if that is what you have.
  5. Cover the dish and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover it and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges.
  6. Garnish with fresh parsley and a little grated parmesan. Let the lasagna rest at least 5 minutes before you slice it, or the layers will slide apart on you.
prose.portion_html: Lasagna is where good intentions go to die, because everybody cuts it by eye and ends up with one heavyweight corner and a row of sad slivers. We do not eyeball it. Once the dish has rested, weigh the whole baked lasagna, subtract the weight of the empty dish you jotted down before you started, and divide what is left by 14. That number is your target per container. Cut and plate to that weight, nudging the last couple of pieces to even things out, and all 14 meals carry the same 496 calories and 40.7 grams of protein. Same portion, same numbers, no guessing on a Tuesday night.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is the part that matters when the receipt prints. Fourteen dinners of chicken alfredo lasagna come out to ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a plate of creamy, cheesy, high-protein comfort food for the price of a drive-thru side, and you built it out of cottage cheese and a jar of sauce. Over 40 grams of protein and under 500 calories, sitting in a container, waiting for you all week.

steps: Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites according to the package, then roughly chop into bite-size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, and a pinch of salt and pepper until completely smooth.

Spread a thin layer of blended sauce in the baking dish, then layer 3 noodle sheets, sauce, chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan; repeat, using parsley only on the first two layers and finishing the top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, then rest at least 5 minutes before slicing.
